explanation: Green's Problem 15: is there a Lipschitz f : ℕ → ℤ whose graph {(n, f(n))} ⊂ ℤ² contains no 3-term progression? LipschitzWith K uses the standard metrics on ℕ and ℤ, so it means |f(n+1) − f(n)| ≤ K. IsAPOfLengthFree … 3 forbids nontrivial 3-APs in ℤ² (the AP sets must have exactly 3 elements). Green writes the graph over n ∈ ℤ, which is a typo given the domain ℕ; the formalization uses ℕ, which is the right reading. The statement is faithful and open.
